question.text: For CBDT purposes, income from transfer of UNLISTED shares is generally treated as:

answer.text: Generally Capital Gains irrespective of holding (per CBDT Letter F.No. 225/12/2016), subject to limited exceptions

explanation.text: The Logic: The CBDT clarification (Letter F.No. 225/12/2016/ITA.II) provides that income from transfer of unlisted shares is generally treated as Capital Gains irrespective of holding period. The Trap: The capital-gains treatment is subject to exceptions — it does not apply where genuineness of the transaction is questionable, where the corporate veil is being misused, or where the transfer is along with control and management of the underlying business. Note: Source: NISM-Series-XIX-B AIF (Cat III) Distributors workbook, pp.308-309, citing CBDT Letter F.No. 225/12/2016/ITA.II.
